sections.theory:
Exercise

Q1. Choose the correct option from the given options.

1. The diamagnetic ion is

a. Ni²⁺

b. Cr³⁺

c. Mn²⁺

d. Cu⁺

2. Potassium ferrocyanide is a

a. normal salt.

b. mixed salt.

c. double salt.

d. complex salt.

3. The co-ordination compound [CuCl₄]²⁻ exists in the shape of

a. tetrahedral.

b. octahedral.

c. square planner.

d. rhombic.

4. The oxidation state of chromium in CrO₂Cl₂ is

a. +2

b. +3

c. +4

d. +6

5. [BeF₄]²⁻ is an example of

a. square planar

b. tetrahedral complex

c. bent structure

d. octahedral complex

6. Which of the following is a typical transition element

a. Zn

b. Cd

c. Ra

d. Co

7. The paramagnetic nature of a substance depends on

a. the number of electron in the outer most orbit.

b. the number of electron that are easily ejected.

c. the number of un-paired electrons.

d. the number of lone pair of electrons.

8. Ligands are

a. electron pair donors.

b. electron pair acceptors.

c. neutral.

d. donor and then acceptor.

9. Which one is not ferromagnetic?

a. Fe

b. Co

c. Sb

d. Ni

10. The co-ordination number of iron in [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻ is

a. 9

b. 3

c. 4

d. 6

11. Select ligand which is bidentate?

a. H₂O

b. NH₃

c. CO

d. C₂O₄²⁻

12. Cu²⁺ salt solution is blue in colour due to transition of electron from

a. s to p orbital.

b. d to d orbital.

c. p to d orbital.

d. p to p orbital.

13. Potassium dichromate acts as a strong

a. oxidizing agent.

b. reducing agent.

c. bleaching agent.

d. dehydrating agent.

14. One of the constituent of German silver is

a. Ag

b. Au

c. Cu

d. Al

15. The names which remains unchanged in naming co-ordination compounds are

a. anionic ligands.

b. cationic ligands.

c. neutral ligands.

d. none of these.

Q2. Write short answers of the following questions.

i. Give the reason that why Cu⁺ is diamagnetic but Cu²⁺ is paramagnetic.

ii. Write down the electronic configuration of the first transition series.

iii. Why the transition elements show the catalytic behaviour?

iv. Give the reason that transition elements form the co-ordination compounds.

v. Explain why transition metals have variable oxidation states.

vi. Justify the statement that “Scandium forms colourless and diamagnetic compounds”.

vii. How do transition elements differ from s and p-block elements?

viii. What is the oxidation state of chromium in [Cr(H₂O)₆]³⁺?

ix. Give the reason that Fe is a catalyst in Haber process but not in the preparation of sulphuric acid.

x. Zn²⁺ salts are white while Cu²⁺ salts are coloured. Why?

Q3. Write detail answers of the following questions.

1. (a). Write down the electronic structure of 3d elements.

(b). Explain why the electronic configuration for chromium and copper differ from those assigned using the Aufbau principle.

2. (a). Explain the origin of colour in coordination compounds

(b). What are the general characteristics of transition elements?

(c). Assess the catalytic nature of vanadium and iron.

3. Discuss in detail the nomenclature of co-ordination compounds with suitable examples.

4. (a). Explain and write the reactions of Potassium Manganate (VII) as an oxidizing agent in organic chemistry.

(b). What are alloys? Describe some properties of an alloy that are different from the metals that compose it.

Exercise

Q1. Choose the correct option from the given options.

1. The diamagnetic ion is

a. Ni²⁺

b. Cr³⁺

c. Mn²⁺

d. Cu⁺

2. Potassium ferrocyanide is a

a. normal salt.

b. mixed salt.

c. double salt.

d. complex salt.

3. The co-ordination compound [CuCl₄]²⁻ exists in the shape of

a. tetrahedral.

b. octahedral.

c. square planner.

d. rhombic.

4. The oxidation state of chromium in CrO₂Cl₂ is

a. +2

b. +3

c. +4

d. +6

5. [BeF₄]²⁻ is an example of

a. square planar

b. tetrahedral complex

c. bent structure

d. octahedral complex

6. Which of the following is a typical transition element

a. Zn

b. Cd

c. Ra

d. Co

7. The paramagnetic nature of a substance depends on

a. the number of electron in the outer most orbit.

b. the number of electron that are easily ejected.

c. the number of un-paired electrons.

d. the number of lone pair of electrons.

8. Ligands are

a. electron pair donors.

b. electron pair acceptors.
